start.penguins: Big news: the boarded-up back of the arcade is getting two new cabinets. Workers start today; that corner's taped off for three days. Keep your tickets warm! - The {hall} front desk
start.gangsters: Word from the {hall}: the back room's getting two new cabinets. Crew's in from today, that corner's taped off three days. Keep your tickets warm. - Front desk

done.penguins: The arcade wing is open! {games} are plugged in and waiting. First one to top the board gets their name on the wall. - The {hall} front desk
done.gangsters: Back room's open. {games} are plugged in. Top the board and your initials go on the wall. - Front desk

start.penguins: The empty corner by the snack bar is becoming a Snowball Roll alley! Four days of sawing and sanding, so mind the dust. - The {hall} front desk
start.gangsters: The dead corner by the snack bar's becoming Alley Roll lanes. Four days of sawing. Mind the dust. - Front desk

done.penguins: Snowball Roll Alley is open! Roll for the hundred hole. Tickets pour out of these things. - The {hall} front desk
done.gangsters: Alley Roll Lanes are open. Aim for the hundred hole. These machines spit tickets. - Front desk

start.penguins: We found a jukebox in the old hotel cellar! Gideon is rewiring it and we're building a little lounge around it. Three days. - The {hall} front desk
start.gangsters: Found a jukebox in the hotel cellar. Gideon's rewiring it, we're building a lounge round it. Three days. - Front desk

done.penguins: The jukebox lounge is open: pick a record, any record, and it plays all day. - The {hall} front desk
done.gangsters: Jukebox lounge is open. Pick a record and the whole hall hears it all day. - Front desk

start.penguins: The prize counter is growing a whole new glass case for our grandest prizes. Four days of polishing. Start saving! - The {hall} front desk
start.gangsters: Prize counter's getting a new glass case for the big prizes. Four days. Start saving. - Front desk

done.penguins: The prize gallery is open: our grandest prizes, under glass, waiting for the very best players. - The {hall} front desk
done.gangsters: Prize gallery's open. The big prizes, under glass. Only serious players need apply. - Front desk

start.penguins: Last big job on the list: the upstairs landing becomes a trophy hall, ready for the first Rec Cup. Five days of work. - The {hall} front desk
start.gangsters: Last big job on the list: the upstairs landing's becoming a trophy hall for the first Rec Cup. Five days. - Front desk

done.penguins: The trophy hall is open, and with it the Rec Cup: every season, beat the posted score and win the cup's tickets. Watch your mail. - The {hall} front desk
done.gangsters: Trophy hall's open, and so is the Rec Cup. Every season, beat the posted score and take the pot. Watch your mail. - Front desk

cab: Shh. I'm on a streak. {game} can smell fear.
One more go on {game} and then I'll go home. That was four goes ago.
If you want {game}, just ask. I'll watch. I'm a great watcher.
lane: Lane's warm. Want to bowl a game together? Loser buys the Fizzy Pop.
Bowling's better with company. Grab a ball and join me.
I'm just practising. ...Okay, I'm losing to myself.
lobby: I came for the games. I'm staying for the sofa.
Best seat in the house is right here. You see everyone's face when they miss.
Somebody won the big teddy last week. The whole room clapped.

chat_league: League night! Two to a lane, and lane four's kept for walk-ins.
League's friendly. Mostly. Gideon keeps a notebook.
Bowl a game with us if you like. No dues, just bragging rights.

gideon: League night. Maple's ahead by six pins. Six. I counted twice.
Steady hands, steady line. Same as the anvil.
maple: League night, dear. I'm defending the cup. Again.
Gideon thinks I can't hear him counting. I can.
finn: League's like a good tide. Comes round every week whether you're ready or not.
ivy: I've got everyone's averages on paper. Mine's improving. Slowly. Measurably.
benno: League night's the one night the horses go to bed without me.

chat_rain: Rain all day, so here we all are. Best roof in town.
Listen to it hammering on the roof! Nobody's going home till it stops.
Rainy days are rec days. Everybody knows that.

_: {you} to {them}! You win this one. I want a rematch.
{them} to your {you}. Good game though. Same time next week?
{you} each! A dead heat. That never happens.
maple: {you} to {them}... well. Don't tell Gideon, dear.
{them} to {you}. The cup stays on my shelf. Lovely game.
A tie! I'll take it. Gideon won't.
gideon: {you} to {them}. Hm. Good line. I'll be practising.
{them} to {you}. Weight, line, follow through. You'll get there.
Even at {you}. Like two halves of a horseshoe.
tobin: {them} to {you}! I WON! Tell everyone. Tell Pip.
Same score! That means I win. That's the rule.

day_words.rest: a rest day (the 6th and 7th of each week)

chat_any: Have you been to the {hall} yet? I keep hearing pins in my sleep.
League night at the {hall}. Half the town goes, the other half pretends not to care.
The prize counter has a teddy bear the size of a toddler. I'm just saying.
chat_soon: Hammering at the old hotel by the library all week. The banner says {hall}. Mayor Alder won't stop grinning.
Somebody carried a whole crate of bowling pins down the avenue. Bowling! Here!
The old hotel south-east of the library is getting a new roof. They say it opens in a few days.
chat_soon_gang: Crews have been in and out of that old hotel by the library all week. Banner says {hall}. Bowling, apparently.
Sal says the old hotel's turning into a place where nobody brings heat. I'll believe it when I see it.
Somebody wheeled six arcade cabinets past the library at dawn. Something's opening south-east of there.

alder: The old hotel's getting a second life. Bowling lanes! Don't tell anyone I picked the carpet.
gideon: Somebody ordered forty brass hinges for that old hotel. Forty. I'm not complaining.
tess: I built the shoe racks for that hotel place. Size 2 to size 14. Somebody here has size 14 feet.
benno: Carted a load of pins up from the beach road for the hotel lot. The horses didn't care for the noise.
hazel: Mabel's been counting days till the hotel opens. She's at four. She's been at four for a week.
sal: Whatever's going into that old hotel, it's loud. I'm told that's the point.

chat_score: Somebody said you bowled a {best}. Was that you? Respect.
Your name's on the high score board. {best}. Don't let it go to your head.

pip: I'm saving tickets for the kite. Don't tell Mabel, she wants it too.
Block Jumper is easy. I mean, I haven't beaten it. But it's easy.
tobin: I bowled a strike once. Okay, it was a gutter that bounced. Still counts.
Bet you can't beat my high score! ...What is my high score? I forgot.
mabel: The teddy bear at the prize counter has a little bow. A LITTLE BOW.
Mum says tickets aren't money. Mum has never seen the prize counter.
wren_jr: Mum says if I get a strike she'll make pancakes. I've had a lot of not-pancakes.
The machines upstairs talk when you win. Mostly they say TRY AGAIN.
gideon: Bowling's just smithing with a ball. Weight, line, follow through.
Maple thinks she's the league champion. Maple is the league champion. Don't tell her I said it.
maple: League night is the only night Gideon's quiet. He's concentrating.
I bowl with my grandmother's ball. It's heavier than it looks, dear. So am I.
finn: Bowling's like casting. Pick a line and trust it.
The lanes are oiled like a calm sea. Ball goes straight till it doesn't.
sal: Late at the {hall}'s the quiet part. Just me and the cabinets.
I don't do prizes. I do high scores. Initials and everything.
lumi: The colors in there! I've been sketching the neon all week.
A rainy day and the {hall}: the best kind of afternoon.
theo: I've charted the pin physics. Theoretically I should bowl 300. Practically: 74.
Every cabinet has a pattern. Learn the pattern, beat the game.
ivy: I keep score on paper. The machine's never wrong, but paper feels right.
Tickets are a currency with zero interest. I've done the maths.
alder: Cutting that ribbon was the proudest morning of my term. Well. One of them.
A town needs a place to gather that isn't the inn. The {hall} is that place.
juniper: Bend your knees when you bowl. I've seen the alternative. It's my whole job.
My one night off and I spend it at lane one. Worth it.
posy: I bring cookies to the {hall} on the weekend. The kids find me in seconds.
The cotton candy is a crime against baking. I had three.
benno: The horses don't care for the pins. I go alone.
Rolled a 140 once. Haven't stopped talking about it, they tell me.
hazel: Rain on the fields, so I'm at the {hall}. Don't look at me like that.
I don't bowl. I watch. It's the same thing with less effort.
rook: Tracking a bowling ball's easy. It only goes one way.
Quiet up there on a weeknight. I like the thunder of it.

alder: A town needs a place to gather where nobody asks questions. The Rec Hall's that place.
No heat inside. That's the rule. Even the President's people bowl badly.
sal: Late at the Rec Hall's the quiet part. Nobody's looking for anybody in there.
I don't do prizes. I do high scores. Initials and everything.
gideon: Bowling's just smithing with a ball. Weight, line, follow through. Same as anything you mean to land.
Maple's beaten me eleven league nights straight. That doesn't leave this hall.
maple: League night's the one night nobody in this town talks business. House rule, and I enforce it.
I bowl with my grandmother's ball, dear. It's seen rougher streets than these.
finn: Bowling's like casting. Pick a line, trust it, don't look back.
Lane four pulls left. Everybody knows. Nobody fixes it. That's this town all over.
lumi: Pink neon on old brick. Only honest light in town. I've filled a sketchbook.
A rainy afternoon at the {hall}. Nobody watching anybody. Best kind of quiet.
theo: I've charted the pin physics. Theory says 300. The lanes say 74.
Every cabinet has a pattern. Learn it and the machine works for you. Rare thing, in this town.
ivy: Tickets earn no interest and nobody can fake them. Cleanest money in the valley.
I keep score on paper. Machines get fixed. Paper remembers.
juniper: Bend your knees when you bowl. Half my Monday patients didn't.
One night off a week, and I spend it on lane one. Nobody here needs patching up. Usually.
posy: I bring cookies at the weekend. Even the tough kids say thank you. Mostly.
The cotton candy is a crime against baking. I had three. Don't tell the crews.
benno: The horses don't care for the pins. I come alone, back lane, nobody bothers me.
Rolled a 140 once. It's chalked on the house wall. Only record of mine I'll ever want.
hazel: Rain on the lot, so I'm at the {hall}. Even gardeners get a night off.
I don't bowl. I watch who sits with who. You learn a lot that way.
rook: A bowling ball only goes one way. Easiest thing in town to track.
Quiet up there on a weeknight. The pins cover any conversation you'd rather keep.
